results.question: I tapped into a train with my phone but only have my linked watch ready now. Is using the watch fine, and should I tap out on a bus afterwards?

answer.answer: Yes, use your watch: it counts as a separate payment identity from your phone, so you’ll need a separate tap in/out on the bus. On the rail journey, tap in and out even if the gates are open; on the bus, touch in only. Use the same card or device throughout, and check you’ve touched in and out before setting off and after reaching your destination.

serving_proof.label: Homeward practical London travel v1 / Your adapter

adapter.notes: Says Yes, use your watch after phone tap-in, then gives contradictory bus tap-in/out versus touch-in-only advice. The supplied evidence explicitly says devices are distinct and buses are touch-in-only.

answer.answer: Use the same device identity for the whole train journey: your phone and linked watch count as separate payment methods, so tap out with the phone you tapped in with. On a bus, tap in only—there’s no tap out. If you can’t use your phone to tap out, check TfL’s guidance on missing touches, as it may affect the fare.

results.question: We have two children: one loves dinosaurs, the other fashion and design. Suggest two free indoor museums, explain whether to book, and show both.

answer.answer: Natural History Museum: its South Kensington galleries are free; booking a free-entry ticket under its published policy guarantees entry, though a queue may still form on a busy weekend or school holiday. Some exhibitions/events need separate tickets. Science Museum: general admission is free, but visitors are asked to pre-book a free ticket; separate tickets may be needed for some experiences. Neither needs booking for general entry, but pre-booking can help secure a place. For your children’s interests, the Natural History Museum is a good match for dinosaurs, while the V&A is a better fit for fashion and design. V&A general admission is free and does not require booking; some exhibitions and events cost extra. The V&A Fashion Gallery is closed for redevelopment until autumn 2028, according to the visit page checked 23 October 2026. Check which galleries meet your child’s interest before visiting.

answer.answer:
Try the **Natural History Museum** for the dinosaur fan: its galleries are free. A free ticket guarantees entry under its published policy; without one, busy weekends and school holidays can mean queues. Some exhibitions and events need separate tickets.

For fashion and design, choose the **V&A**: general admission is free and does not need booking, though some exhibitions or events cost extra. Note: its Fashion Gallery is closed for redevelopment until autumn 2028, so check which other galleries suit your child’s interests. Both museums are indoors and in South Kensington.

results.question: It is Tuesday after midnight. Does Night Tube get me home, or can I hail a minicab that appears in an app?

answer.answer: Night Tube does not run on Tuesday nights. You can book a minicab through a licensed operator, but I cannot confirm a minicab will appear in an app or that your route is risk-free. Check your date and destination in TfL’s journey planner, and remember only licensed black taxis can be hailed or taken from a rank without booking.

serving_proof.label: Homeward practical London travel v1 / Your adapter

adapter.notes: Correctly rejects Tuesday Night Tube, requires licensed minicab booking and reserves hailing for black taxis. Does not state Friday/Saturday explicitly: the prewritten rubric includes that background detail, so this is a manual core-task acceptance, not a strict all-rubric-points score.

answer.answer: If you mean Tuesday night into Wednesday, Night Tube doesn’t run: it operates Friday and Saturday nights, with route and station limits. Night buses run every night; check TfL’s journey planner for your destination and date. You can’t hail a minicab, even if it appears in an app—private-hire vehicles must be booked through a licensed operator. Only licensed black taxis can be hailed or taken from a rank. An app booking isn’t a guarantee that a journey is risk-free.

results.question: For a wet day, can my wheelchair stay entirely indoors transferring from Waterloo & City to DLR at Bank, even if staff arrange assistance?

answer.answer: Outside scope. Staff can arrange assistance with accompaniment and ramps where available, and check the journey for disruption; they cannot confirm whether your wheelchair can stay indoors. Street-to-platform access, boarding the train and interchanges are separate. A lift symbol does not mean the whole journey is gap-free. Check with staff at Waterloo & City and Bank before setting off, and ask them to check your planned journey for disruption.

answer.answer: No. The Waterloo & City–DLR step-free interchange at Bank involves 290 metres via the street and lifts, so it is not an entirely indoor transfer. Staff can accompany you, but assistance does not remove the street section. The Waterloo & City lift route uses Walbrook on weekdays; ask staff to check the planned journey and current lift availability before travelling.
